findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false and its flag check is misleading
findings.body: The helper always returns false. `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)` names the disabled state 'enabled', and both branches return false, so the flag lookup has no effect on the result. This is a security gate, and the inverted naming makes it easy to misread or to 'fix' later by flipping the wrong condition. It also adds a dereference of h.features on the SQL path, which previously never touched the feature toggles, so a reader constructed with nil features would now panic on any SQL expression instead of returning the intended error. A plain hard-coded rejection with a comment explaining the disable would make the intent obvious.

findings.title: SQL command construction and execution have no disable gate of their own
findings.body: The only enforcement of the disable is the new check in ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery (reader.go). NewSQLCommand, the exported UnmarshalSQLCommand, and SQLCommand.Execute remain callable with no check. The current safety depends entirely on the stub in pkg/expr/sql/db.go returning 'not implemented' from TablesList/QueryFramesInto. Any caller that builds a SQLCommand without going through ReadQuery, or any future change that reimplements the DB stub, reopens the RCE/LFI path the PR is closing, with no second check to catch it. The disable should also be enforced at the command boundary (for example in NewSQLCommand or Execute) so the protection does not rest on one stub's error return.

findings.title: No test covers the rejection of SQL expressions and no test files were updated
findings.body: This security fix adds a new early return for QueryTypeSQL but no test asserts that a SQL expression query is rejected, with or without the sqlExpressions flag. None of the changed files are test files. Existing tests for sql.TablesList, NewSQLCommand, or SQLCommand.Execute, if any exist, previously exercised DuckDB behaviour and will now fail against the stub, and nothing in the PR updates them. A regression test for the reader rejection is needed so that re-enabling the path cannot happen silently.

findings.title: sqlExpressions flag is now a no-op, but its documented meaning and error text are inconsistent with that
findings.body: After this change, enabling the sqlExpressions feature flag does nothing: every SQL expression is rejected with 'sqlExpressions is not implemented'. The flag is still registered and documented as enabling SQL expressions, which the PR description acknowledges it is leaving unchanged. Users who enable the flag will get an error that points at the flag as if it were the problem, and operators reading the flag docs will be misled. At minimum the flag description and this message should say that SQL expressions are disabled for security reasons regardless of the flag.
